FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving vision means spotting hazards under changing light, judging gaps, matching traffic speed, and reading signs [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Drivers must hear horns, sirens, motorcycles, and screeching tires, and wearing a headset or earplugs in both ears is illegal [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Fatigue and drowsiness degrade vision and slow reactions to hazards [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Stay alert enough to pick the right move fast in every traffic situation, surprises included [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can make a driver unsafe, sometimes through sleepiness, so learn every medication's effects [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
Physicians must report patients aged fourteen and up whose medical conditions, such as lapse of consciousness, could impair safe driving [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
Keep both hands on the wheel whenever possible [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
Hand-to-hand push-pull steering starts at 9 and 3 o'clock or 8 and 4 o'clock, never crosses hands past the wheel's center, and holds those spots through turns [A01].
Why it matters: the no-crossing rule is what separates push-pull from hand-over-hand.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A02
Hand-over-hand fits low-speed turns, parking, and skid recovery [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A02
Its sequence runs: start at 8 and 4 o'clock, reach across to the far side, release the other hand, then reach across the gripping arm and pull up [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A02
One hand suffices when turning while backing to watch behind, with that hand at the 12 o'clock spot [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A02
One hand also suffices when working a control that forces a hand off the wheel [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A02
Signals, horn, and headlights speak to fellow drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
Signal every turn, lane change, slowdown, and stop with lamps or hand-and-arm positions, using arm signals when lamps fail or harsh sun hides them [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists may mark a turn by extending one arm straight toward that side [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A03
Signal at least one hundred feet before turns, ahead of every lane change, and at least five seconds before freeway lane changes [A03].
Why it matters: one hundred feet and five seconds are the two signal numbers to memorize.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A03
Also signal curb pull-ins and pull-outs, empty-looking roads, and late-through-the-intersection turns coming right after it [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A03
Switch the signal off once it has served its purpose [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A03
Sound the horn to announce presence or flag danger: to avert collisions and to warn oncoming drivers on narrow mountain roads with under two hundred feet of sight [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A03
Drop from high to low beams within five hundred feet of oncoming traffic and within three hundred feet behind a followed vehicle, since parking-lights-only driving is illegal [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A03
Light up when darkness hides beyond one thousand feet, from thirty minutes after sunset until thirty minutes before sunrise [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A03
Also light low beams for wiper weather, for murk such as clouds, dust, smoke, or fog, for mountain roads and tunnels even in sun, where signs command lights, and to stand out in low sun [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A04
Warn followers of a hazard ahead with flashers, three or four light brake taps, and a hand signal while slowing and stopping [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A04
Trouble stops start with flashers, or turn signals if flashers are missing, plus pulling fully off the road clear of traffic [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A04
When fully clear is impossible, stop where drivers behind can see car and driver, never just past a hill crest or curve [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A04
Call for roadside rescue and wait inside the vehicle until it comes [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
